chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And sent against them birds in flocks'

'Striking them with stones of baked clay.' He said: 'These were low-flying birds that came to them from the sea. Their heads were like the heads of predatory beasts, and their claws were like the claws of predatory beasts among birds. With each bird were three stones: two in its legs and one in its beak. So it kept striking them with them until their bodies became covered in smallpox blisters, and killed them with them. And before that, nothing of smallpox had been seen, nor did they see such birds before that day, nor after it.'
He said: 'And whoever escaped from them on that day went forth until they reached Hazramaut, which is a valley below Yemen. Allah sent a flood against them and drowned them all.'
He said: 'And no water had been seen in that valley at all for fifteen years before that day.'
He said: 'Therefore, it was named Hazramaut (Death Arrived) when they died in it.'

key_terms.حَضْرَمَوْتَ: A valley in Yemen, meaning 'Death Arrived'

ai.seo_question: What were the characteristics of the birds sent against the people of the Elephant according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a unique exegetical perspective on the Ababil birds by detailing their physical attributes and the specific mechanism of their attack, emphasizing the miraculous nature of the event through the sudden appearance of water in the dry valley of Hazramaut. It highlights the comprehensive divine punishment, linking the aerial assault with the subsequent drowning of survivors, thereby reinforcing the concept of Allah's absolute power over natural elements as a sign for the people of the Elephant.
